title: Director of Sales

role_match.role_rationale_from_stage3: Mimaki's distribution model through dealers and direct sales to print service providers means the Director of Sales is accountable for revenue growth, dealer satisfaction, and closing enterprise accounts. Sales reps constantly face objections around total cost of ownership, durability concerns, and competitive pressure from lower-cost alternatives. Offering Tedlar as a recommended overlaminate solution gives sales teams a defensible premium story: instead of competing on printer price alone, they can sell a complete durability system with quantifiable ROI (fewer reprints, reduced maintenance, extended graphic lifespan). For vehicle wrap shops and outdoor signage companies—Mimaki's core customers—graffiti resistance and 20+ year durability directly translate to lower callbacks and higher customer retention. This role cares about deal velocity, win rates against competitors, and upsell attachment rates. Tedlar becomes an upsell opportunity and competitive differentiator, particularly when pursuing municipal contracts, transit authorities, and fleet graphics customers who prioritize lifecycle cost over initial price. With 160+ employees across multiple training centers, equipping the sales organization with Tedlar's value story directly impacts quota attainment.

engagement_strategy.scope_and_authority: As Director of Sales, [Name] owns revenue targets, dealer relationships, and sales team performance across Mimaki's North American operations spanning 160+ employees in five training centers. They manage both direct sales to print service providers and indirect channel sales through dealers. This role directly influences which consumables and solutions get recommended alongside Mimaki's printer systems, controls sales enablement and training programs, and determines go-to-market strategy for competitive positioning. They report to senior leadership (likely VP Sales or GM) and manage regional sales managers and account executives who face daily pricing and durability objections from vehicle wrap shops and signage companies.
engagement_strategy.relevant_use_cases: Vehicle wraps and fleet graphics represent Mimaki's core application—Tedlar's graffiti resistance means wrap shops can offer vandalism protection to municipal fleets and transit authorities, reducing callback costs and warranty claims. For outdoor signage customers using Mimaki's eco-solvent printers, Tedlar extends graphic lifespan beyond typical 3-5 year expectations to 12-20+ years, allowing print service providers to offer premium pricing tiers and extended service contracts. Architectural graphics and building wraps—particularly for the new Flowery Branch showroom facility—benefit from Tedlar's UV protection and weather resistance (-70°F to 230°F), creating demonstration opportunities. The sales team can position Mimaki + Tedlar as a complete system solution rather than competing on printer cost alone, particularly valuable when facing lower-priced Chinese printer manufacturers.
engagement_strategy.personal_stakes: [Name] is measured on quarterly revenue growth, win rate against competitors (Roland, HP, Epson), dealer satisfaction scores, and attachment rates for consumables and accessories. Their personal pain points include: sales reps losing deals on price because they can't articulate value beyond initial equipment cost; customer complaints about premature fading or cracking that damage Mimaki's reputation and dealer relationships; difficulty differentiating Mimaki's eco-solvent printers in a commoditizing market; and pressure to increase revenue per transaction. Tedlar directly addresses these by providing concrete ROI arguments (fewer replacements = lower total cost), reducing post-sale warranty issues that strain dealer relationships, creating a premium positioning story that justifies higher prices, and offering an upsell opportunity that increases average deal size without requiring new customer acquisition.
engagement_strategy.timing_factors: Mimaki exhibited at ISA Sign Expo in Las Vegas (April 23-25, 2025) and ISA 2026 in Orlando, making NOW an opportune moment to discuss how Tedlar could strengthen their trade show positioning for future events. Their JFX200-1213 EX won a 2025 Pinnacle Award from PRINTING United Alliance, creating momentum around innovation and quality messaging. The June 2025 opening of the new Flowery Branch corporate office with expanded showroom presents a physical demonstration opportunity—Tedlar-protected graphics in the showroom itself would provide proof of performance. With 25 years of service celebrated in 2024, Mimaki is emphasizing heritage and reliability, which aligns perfectly with Tedlar's proven track record. The launch of the JV200 Series emphasizing 'industry's best outdoor color durability' suggests active product differentiation efforts that Tedlar could amplify.

personalization_hooks.hook: Mimaki's sales teams face constant total cost of ownership objections from vehicle wrap shops and signage companies evaluating eco-solvent printer purchases
personalization_hooks.messaging_angle: Position Tedlar as the competitive answer that transforms pricing conversations—instead of defending printer cost, sales reps can sell a complete protection system with quantifiable ROI. Frame this as arming their 160+ person sales organization with a tool to close deals they're currently losing on price.

personalization_hooks.hook: Mimaki partners with 3M's MCS Warranty Program and explicitly markets 'industry's best outdoor color durability' with the JV200 Series
personalization_hooks.messaging_angle: Acknowledge their existing durability focus and suggest Tedlar as the logical extension—if they're already promising best-in-class outdoor performance, Tedlar provides the overlaminate solution that backs up that claim with measurable results. Reference their 3M partnership as proof they understand warranty value.

personalization_hooks.hook: Their dealer network and print service provider customers constantly face graffiti vandalism on installed vehicle wraps and outdoor signage, leading to costly reprints and customer dissatisfaction
personalization_hooks.messaging_angle: Lead with the graffiti resistance story specifically—spray paint and permanent marker wipe off Tedlar-protected graphics, eliminating a major pain point for municipal fleet customers and transit authorities. This creates a defensible premium tier that dealers can sell at higher margins while reducing their own warranty exposure.

recommended_approach: Lead with the competitive differentiation and revenue impact angle. Open by acknowledging Mimaki's strong market position and recent awards, then quickly pivot to the sales challenge: price competition and total cost objections. Position Tedlar not as a material specification but as a sales enablement tool that transforms how their teams compete. Include a specific offer: 'I'd like to share how three comparable printer manufacturers are using Tedlar to win fleet graphics contracts they previously lost on price.' This frames the conversation as peer benchmarking rather than vendor pitching, and appeals directly to [Name]'s need to improve win rates and deal velocity.
